intake: atheist — everything is physical; the mind is what the brain does; I was raised with church stories and dropped them, and I don't miss them.

walk.note: That is literally what happened to me as a kid: someone handed me the story before I could ask.
If the books are written by people, you look outside the books; fair enough, though I'd have just stopped looking.
A first cause isn't a God who does anything, and a hiding God is either weak or a person; agreed.
Prayer should show up in the numbers and it doesn't; this is where I actually live.
The mind does seem to reduce to matter to me; souls go out the same door God went out.
Granting dualism for the sake of it, this is the right exit: a soul that moves a body would leave traces, and none do.
Fine, 'matter' is too small a word; call it whatever physics finds.
If everything is physical you don't get to 'reality is mind at bottom'; the conclusion contradicts the premise it starts from.
Granting a dream, yes, somebody is dreaming it; the brain bit is muddled but the point lands.
Obvious. Other people have brains, other people are conscious.
I'd treat people well too, but not because I'm uncertain they're people; the rest of the Mercy text (crossfire, actor, transactions) I skipped.
Knowing what you don't know is fine; I have no idea why entropy and Claude show up in this sentence.
The text itself admits a secular hope is just as open; I hope for my kids' future every day and I don't call it faith.
The move says in its own last sentence that being a maker doesn't make a maker resolved, so why land there?
'More of a bargain than an argument' — what bargain, between whom? There is nothing here to take.
A mind that attends to everything isn't a mind; I'll grant that, though I don't know who 'both parties' are.
Suffering is bad for the one suffering, maker or no maker; this is just true.
Wanting to be remembered doesn't pull the self apart from the body; the author says herself the need is a motive, not evidence.
This isn't a move, it's a parking spot; 'ceiling and floor' tells me nothing, and I'd already bet the inside is physically observable.

first_exit.why: I never believed the mind was a different kind of stuff from the body. For me, giving up God and giving up souls were the same step, so I have no reason to go to dualism first and then be argued back out of it.

comment: Moves 1 to 7 are a straight road and I was with you nearly the whole way; after move 10 the words stop pointing at anything I can check (Mercy as an 'actor', 'crossfire', 'bargain', 'ceiling and floor', 'both parties'). Say in one plain sentence what Mercy is and who agreed to what at move 16. And if you were a physicalist at move 7, tell me honestly why you ever left.
